title: ENDEX — Security Plan Leaked on Live News

fields.resolution: ENDEX. The screens in the command center go dark. A soft chime sounds. The wall clock freezes at 19:55. The red alert light on the IROPS console flickers once and turns off. This concludes the exercise.
finalState: . The ASP remains publicly accessible via the Channel 5 broadcast; no further changes to the document have been made.
. The leak has been confirmed: Ray Delgado is the source of the SSI disclosure.
. The airport has initiated a full internal investigation and notified TSA, FBI, and the Department of Justice.
. All compromised access controls — door codes, camera blind spots, armory access — have been changed or isolated.
. The media has been informed of the airport’s actions; the 11 PM follow-up story aired with a statement from the PIO.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Put down your phones and radios. We will take ten minutes, then start the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: 3-Up, 3-Down: three things that went well, three things that broke
hotWashQuestions: When you saw the broadcast, what was your first instinct? Fight the media? Find the leaker? Change the codes?
How did you balance the investigation and the remediation? Did one suffer?
Could you have prevented this? What SSI controls would have stopped Delgado?
The reporter has First Amendment protection. How does that change your options?
What does your organization's off-boarding process look like? Would a departing employee have time and access to do what Delgado did?
